subject: Fall 2020 School Reopening Plan
overview: Medford Public Schools administrators held a public Q&A session to outline state COVID-19 metrics and answer community questions regarding fall 2020 school reopening plans. District leaders addressed hybrid and remote learning choices, safety and health protocols, HVAC evaluations, special education, technology platforms, and staff COVID-19 testing.

items.title: State Guidance and COVID-19 Metrics Overview
items.summary: Administrators presented state guidance placing Medford in the green COVID-19 risk category, permitting hybrid or full-time in-person learning options.

items.title: Learning Model Selection and Transfers
items.summary: District leaders explained that families can formally request transfers between hybrid and remote learning models near the end of marking periods, subject to building capacity.

items.title: Teachers Union Negotiations
items.summary: Officials stated that district lawyers and union representatives are scheduling dates to continue impact bargaining negotiations prior to the start of school.

items.title: Staggered Reopening Metrics and Health Protocols
items.summary: Administrators noted that progressing through two-week staggered reopening phases depends on Medford maintaining green or unshaded state health metrics.

items.title: Contingency All-Remote Schedule
items.summary: Officials confirmed that if health conditions force a full school closure, hybrid students will remain with their assigned teachers under a modified remote schedule.

items.title: High-Needs IEP Classifications
items.summary: District leaders clarified that high-needs designations for in-person priority apply to students requiring targeted special education services for approximately 75 percent of their school day.

items.title: Mask Rules and Exemptions
items.summary: Administrators emphasized mandatory mask enforcement across all grades, stating non-compliant students will transfer to remote learning while medically exempted students will use clear desk shields.

items.title: Technology and Software Access
items.summary: District staff announced the deployment of the Clever single sign-on platform to centralize student access to educational software.

items.title: Daily Health Screening App
items.summary: Officials announced a partnership providing free access to the AlphaMed app for daily COVID-19 self-screenings by staff and building visitors.

items.title: Cohort Balancing and Sibling Alignment
items.summary: District leaders explained plans to align schedules for siblings across different schools while balancing class sizes between hybrid cohorts.

items.title: HVAC and Building Ventilation
items.summary: Administrators reported ongoing maintenance to school ventilation units and announced an upcoming engineering evaluation of the high school's HVAC system.

items.title: Course Scheduling, Specials, and Orientations
items.summary: District staff outlined restrictions on music and physical education classes, adding that three planning days will be dedicated to student and family orientations.

items.title: Transportation Limits and Walking Routes
items.summary: Officials highlighted a 68 percent reduction in school bus capacity under distancing guidelines and encouraged parent-led walking school buses.

items.title: Staff PPE and Behavioral Support
items.summary: District staff detailed counseling resources and confirmed that direct-service teachers will receive face shields and protective masks.

items.title: Staff COVID-19 Testing Program
items.summary: School leaders announced biweekly COVID-19 testing for all school district staff through a partnership with Tufts University and the Board of Health.
